_comment: TARGET-tier). One per crustify invocation target. It names the files the
target covers and in which scope, plus a target-local refinement of what
is out of scope. Values below illustrate a run scoped to ssl/statem
inside an openssl checkout; substitute for other projects.
_comment_layout: All crustify artifacts live under a single `crustify/` directory at the
repository root (which also marks the root). REPO-ROOT-tier artifacts are
TARGET-tier artifacts live under crustify/targets/<target>/ and are
invocation-scoped: this scope-config.json, the derived scope.json, and
The repo root and the target id are CLI positionals
under `crustify/targets/<target>/` records the target. Neither is
restated here: a second copy can only drift from the invocation.
_comment_files: The target's file set - everything this invocation covers. Repo-root-
relative, always explicit: there is no implicit directory walk, so this
must name everything the target contains. Entries are either:
* a FILE      - `include/internal/statem.h`
* a DIRECTORY, written with a trailing slash - `ssl/` - which expands
to every source/header file beneath it
The trailing-slash convention matches `out_of_scope.paths` below, and
`out_of_scope` applies to whatever a directory entry expands to.
Naming a file the build never compiled is harmless: scope.json is
anchored on the T1 tables, so uncompiled candidates simply drop out.
ONE list, deliberately. Scope says what the target CONTAINS; it does
not say what will be done with it. Port or wrap is the translate
stage's objective, chosen per unit by the orchestrator - an item can
legitimately be wrapped now and ported later, and encoding a verb here
would freeze that choice at scope time.
NAME EVERY FILE THAT DEFINES SOMETHING YOU WANT IN SCOPE. Classification
is DEFINITION-anchored: an entity is in the target iff its BODY lives in a
file named here (or, for a declaration-only entity, all its declarations
do). That one rule cuts both ways, and missing either half silently drops
work:
* THE SOURCES. A function's body is in a .c. Listing only public headers
admits just what they DEFINE - inline functions, macros, value structs
- while every function they merely DECLARE falls out of scope entirely,
its body sitting in a .c you did not name. To wrap a library's public
API, name the library.
* THE HEADERS. A struct, enum or union is DEFINED in a header, and
headers outside the target tree are NEVER discovered automatically. A
public value type whose header you did not name is not in your target,
however much of its implementation is. Add a header only if its
IMPLEMENTORS are in the target - distinguish implementors from
consumers and referencers. A header whose types are merely USED by the
target reaches the import section on its own, through the closure.
Narrowing to an API SURFACE is a selection concern, not a scope one:
`translate --file include/openssl/ssl.h` or `--name`. Keeping the
implementations in scope is what lets the ownership analysis read
free/store/return behaviour off the real bodies instead of guessing
from a signature.
Everything an in-scope entity REACHES but that this list does not name
is an IMPORT - the FFI frontier - derived automatically into
scope.json's sibling `import` section. Nothing needs to name it.
_comment_out_of_scope: Target-local refinement of what crustify must NOT analyze. `paths` lists
repo-root-relative paths (directories with trailing `/` recurse; entries
without are exact-file matches) that the composer skips while expanding
`files`, even when a directory entry there covers them. Project-wide
exclusions (e.g. `apps/`, `fuzz/`) are implicit via not being named in
`files` - list them here only if a directory entry would otherwise pull
them in. `features` lists macro feature names (typically
`OPENSSL_NO_<FEATURE>` or equivalent) the user wants treated as
disabled. NOTE: like `build.json`'s `features` block, this list is
currently DOCUMENTATION ONLY - no composer reads it. Dead code is
filtered implicitly instead: scope.json is anchored on the T1 tables, so
a body elided by a disabled feature contributes no entities and its file
